output.summary: Fast-growing, short-lived tree native to North America from Canada to Honduras. Unlike most maples, it regularly has compound leaves with more than three leaflets, and male and female flowers grow on separate trees. Native American peoples made syrup from its sap and prepared the inner bark as winter food or crystallized sugar.
output.edibilityNote: Native American peoples made syrup and drinks from the sap and prepared inner bark as winter food or crystallized sugar.
